title: read_goal_state injected stale flags persisted by all write paths
description: read_goal_state (mod.rs:129-156) calls annotate_goal_staleness after reading GOAL_STATE.json, injecting ephemeral fields stale/stale_reason into the Value. Five write paths in goal_ops.rs then write the complete Value (including the stale annotations) back to disk: checkpoint(line 508-530), pause/block via set_terminal_flags(line 1057-1091), resume(line 980-1021), complete(line 571-696), continue_review/retry(line 720-738). These ephemeral runtime-only metadata fields leak into persistent state, corrupting GOAL_STATE.json schema purity. Only amend(line 783-940) avoids this because it checks the stale flag and rejects before writing.
recommendation: Strip stale and stale_reason fields before writing in all 5 mutating paths. Either: (1) clear them from the Value object just before write_atomic_json, or (2) introduce a read_raw_goal_state() that skips annotate_goal_staleness and use it for write-oriented reads.

title: complete operation has no state guard at entry
description: The complete path (goal_ops.rs:569-715) reads goal state but never checks current status or the stale flag. Problems: (1) completing a paused goal increments iteration_count while status stays paused - state inconsistency. (2) completing a stale goal from another session is allowed (contrast with amend which explicitly blocks stale at line 807). (3) completing a blocked goal is also allowed. complete is the only mutating operation without any entry guard on current state validity.
recommendation: Add status guard after read (line 571): allow only running/review_pending states for complete, reject paused/blocked. Also add stale guard: reject completed goals that are annotated as stale (session_id mismatch). For review_pending -> complete (currently impossible since review_pending can only exit via retry), this guard would be a safety net.

title: continue_review and retry are semantically identical
description: Lines 716-762 map both 'continue_review' and 'retry' operations to identical code: set status=running, clear blockers, write state, sync pointers. The error message at line 729 only mentions 'retry', and the response operation at line 758 is hardcoded as 'retry'. These operations should have different semantics (continue_review = review approved, proceed; retry = try again after fixing issues), but the implementation does not distinguish them. A caller invoking continue_review receives a response labelled 'retry'.
recommendation: Either remove the continue_review alias entirely (keeping only retry), or implement distinct semantics. If continue_review is retained, it should have matching response labels and distinct behavior such as preserving some review metadata.

title: resume via MCP tool cannot pass drive_until_down flag
description: goal_handler.rs:131 has an empty handler arm for resume. It never forwards the drive_until_done or contract fields (non_goals, done_when, validation_commands) from MCP arguments to the goal_ops payload. The goal_ops resume path (line 558) defaults drive_until_done=true when the field is absent. Therefore all MCP tool resume calls unconditionally set drive_until_done=true, preventing callers from resuming a goal in non-driving mode through the standard tool interface. The test at mod.rs:639-651 ('resume_can_leave_drive_until_done_disabled_when_requested') uses the direct framework_goal_drive API which does forward the field.
recommendation: Add drive_until_done forwarding to the resume arm in goal_handler.rs. Additionally consider forwarding non_goals, done_when, validation_commands if needed for drive-contract revalidation on resume.

title: session staleness not enforced on any operation except amend
description: annotate_goal_staleness (mod.rs:95-126) correctly tags goals with stale=true when session_id mismatches or auto-generated IDs are detected. However the stale flag is only checked by amend (line 807). All other mutating operations - checkpoint(line 508), pause/block(set_terminal_flags), resume(line 980), complete(line 571), continue_review/retry(line 720) - read the flag via read_goal_state but never examine it. A stale goal from another session can have its iteration count inflated, checkpoints appended, or state toggled. Only amend is protected. Combined with GOAL-001, the stale flag itself could also be persisted.
recommendation: Add stale flag check to all mutating operations: checkpoint, pause, block, resume, complete, continue_review/retry. The check pattern already exists at amend line 807; replicate it before state mutation in each operation.

title: QG hook error is fail-open but missing-pass field is fail-closed
description: At line 667-674, when evaluate_quality_gate returns Err, the code warns and continues without the quality gate (fail-open). But at line 624, when evaluate_quality_gate returns Ok(verdict) but the verdict is missing the 'passed' field, it defaults to false (fail-closed). This asymmetry means: a broken QG hook silently allows all completions, while a QG that returns a response missing expected fields blocks them. For maintainability, both error conditions should have consistent behavior.
recommendation: Align the failure modes: either both should fail-open (continue without gate) or both should fail-closed (block the transition). The error path at line 667 should probably propagate the error rather than silently continuing. Consider adding a configuration flag to choose the behavior.

title: QG blocked path writes inconsistent ledger transaction type
description: When QG blocks the completion (lines 631-665), the ledger transaction type is 'goal_state'. But the normal complete path (line 700) writes 'goal_iteration_completed'. These represent different semantic operations: one is a completion attempt that was blocked by quality gate, the other is a successful iteration completion. Using 'goal_state' for the blocked path makes it indistinguishable from a general state update in the ledger timeline.
recommendation: The QG-blocked path should use a distinct transaction type such as 'quality_gate_blocked' or 'iteration_blocked' to enable accurate ledger-based audit and reconstruction.

title: no maximum iteration limit on loop goals
description: The complete operation only increments iteration_count (line 682-686). There is no circuit breaker, maximum iteration count, or automatic escalation when a goal reaches a high iteration count. While this is by design for the loop semantic, a runaway goal could accumulate unbounded iteration_count values and all associated ledger entries. The goal-engine's runner (runner.rs:401-427) has its own circuit breaker and consecutive_failure tracking, but the core-state goal system independently has none.
recommendation: Consider adding an optional max_iterations field to goal state. When exceeded, the complete path would automatically transition the goal to a terminal review_pending state or require explicit override. Alternatively, ensure the loop runner's circuit breaker gracefully handles excessive iteration.

title: amend replaces (not merges) non_goals/done_when/validation_commands
description: Lines 828-854 show that amend does a full replacement of non_goals, done_when, and validation_commands arrays. The caller must provide the complete new list - there is no incremental add/remove mechanism. For a drive_until_done goal with, say, 10 done_when items, adding one more item requires the caller to re-specify all 10 existing items plus the new one. This increases the risk of accidental contract violations and requires the caller to read the full state before amending.
recommendation: Consider adding array merge/append semantics: e.g., a 'merge' flag that appends provided items to existing arrays instead of replacing. Document the current replace-only behavior clearly in the SKILL.md.

title: completed status guard exists but is unreachable from goal_ops operations
description: The set_terminal_flags guard at line 1067 and the amend guard at line 796 both check for status == 'completed' and reject. However, goal_ops' complete operation never sets status to 'completed' - it stays 'running' (line 678 comment: 'Complete = iteration complete, NOT goal termination'). The 'completed' status can only come from legacy paths or manual file edits. These guards are dead branches in the current v10 loop-semantics state machine.
recommendation: Either restore a termination operation (e.g., 'archive' or 'terminate') that sets status='completed' and removes the goal from continuation requests, or remove the dead guard if it is confirmed unreachable in any valid flow.

title: goal-engine runner and core-state goal state maintain independent state files that can diverge
description: goal-engine maintains LOOP_RUN_STATE.json with LoopPhase/run tracking (runner.rs, state.rs), while core-state maintains GOAL_STATE.json with status/iteration_count (goal_ops.rs). The runner only reads GOAL_STATE.json one-way for drift detection (runner.rs:894-906) and never writes to it. Conversely, goal_ops never reads LOOP_RUN_STATE.json. A loop could have 5 iterations in GOAL_STATE.json but a different run count in LOOP_RUN_STATE.json after kills and cleanup. There is no cross-crate reconciliation mechanism.
recommendation: Decide on a single source of truth. Either have the runner update GOAL_STATE.json on each phase transition, or consolidate both states into one file with both loop and goal fields. If the divergence is intentional, document the boundary explicitly and add a health-check that warns when they deviate significantly.

title: checkpoint writes stale-guarded state without staleness check
description: The checkpoint path (line 507-529) reads via read_goal_state (which annotates staleness as ephemeral), appends a checkpoint entry, then writes the entire state back. Like the other mutating paths, it does not check the stale flag (GOAL-005) and would persist any stale annotation (GOAL-001). Additionally, checkpoint is purely additive with no max cap on the checkpoints array length - unbounded growth could occur.
recommendation: Add stale check before checkpoint write. Consider adding a maximum checkpoint count (e.g., 100) to prevent unbounded file growth. Strip ephemeral fields before writing.
